review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the definitions of ParabolicPoint, spatialPartial, timePartial, spatialDeriv, spatialLaplacian and backwardHeatCutoff. I read the statement of caccioppoli_cutoff_heat_timePartial in Terms.lean and the private bridge lemma in Endgame/CutoffDerivatives.lean. The file has no @[simp] attributes of its own, and its local simp_rw uses are terminating rewrites with explicit hypotheses. I found no loops or competing rules. The two findings concern the missing canonical shape and bridge lemmas for the simp set. Both are moderate in strength. I could not run Lean, so I do not claim that the proposed forms compile or that the ParabolicPoint unfolding is the only thing the simpa calls do.

findings.problem: The theorem is stated with eta-expanded lambdas `fun w : ParabolicPoint => backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r w`. That is not the form simp or the neighbouring lemmas use. `caccioppoli_cutoff_heat_timePartial` in Terms.lean is stated as `timePartial (backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r) z`. The mismatch forces `simpa only [ParabolicPoint] using htime` at line 70 and `simpa only [ParabolicPoint] using hht` at lines 362 and 538. These calls pass the definition `ParabolicPoint` to simp as an unfolding rule just to reshape binders. `ParabolicPoint` is a plain `def`, deliberately distinct from `Vec3 × ℝ` because of the parabolic metric, so unfolding it is brittle. Every downstream user, such as the `hht'` restatements, must copy the long lambda form. In the cutoff theorems that copy then needs the same conversion.
findings.proposed_change: State `caccioppoli_I1_heat_operator` in the eta-reduced normal form, for example `timePartial (backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r) z + ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial (backwardHeatCutoff η x₀ t₀ r) i i z = (timePartial η z + ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial η i i z) * ... + 2 * ∑ i, spatialPartial η i z * ...`. Do the same for the `η w` and `caccioppoliCutoff ... w` lambdas. Then delete the `htime'` and `hht'` restatements and the `simpa only [ParabolicPoint]` calls. Use `hht` and `htime` directly in the `rw` and `calc` steps.
findings.benefit: Readers and `rw`/`simp` calls see one canonical shape that matches Terms.lean. The proofs no longer unfold `ParabolicPoint` through simp, and each annulus theorem loses roughly 15 lines of restated hypotheses.

findings.excerpt:
rw [show spatialLaplacian (fun x : Vec3 => η (x, z.2)) z.1 =
      ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial (fun w : ParabolicPoint => η w) i i z by rfl]
findings.problem: The proof moves between the slice-level API (`spatialDeriv`, `spatialLaplacian` on `fun x => f (x, z.2)`) and the point-level API (`spatialPartial`, `spatialSecondPartial`) with one-off local facts. These are `hηpartial` (an `rfl`), `hΓpartial` (via `simpa only [spatialPartial, spatialDeriv]`) and an inline `show … by rfl`. The earlier `hsum` step does the same with `change` followed by `rfl`. The same bridge `spatialLaplacian (fun x => ψ (x, z.2)) z.1 = ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial ψ i i z` is re-proved as a private `rfl` lemma in Endgame/CutoffDerivatives.lean. No public simp-usable lemma exists, so each proof must unfold the definitions or restate the fact. The direction is also hidden: `simp_rw [hΓpartial]` and `simp_rw [hηpartial]` rewrite only because the pattern was restated per call.
findings.proposed_change: Add public bridge lemmas near `spatialPartial` or `LeibnizLaplacian`. One is `spatialDeriv (fun x => g (x, z.2)) i z.1 = spatialPartial g i z`. The other is `spatialLaplacian (fun x => g (x, z.2)) z.1 = ∑ i, spatialSecondPartial g i i z`, with the slice form as the left-hand side. Mark them `@[simp]` only after checking that the left-hand sides do not clash with the existing `spatialDeriv_mul`/`spatialDeriv_add` rules. Otherwise use them via `simp only [...]`/`rw`. Then replace `hηpartial`, the inline `show … by rfl`, and the private `laplacian_eq_sum_second` with these lemmas.
findings.benefit: The slice-to-point conversion gets one canonical oriented rule instead of per-proof `rfl` restatements. This removes duplication between I1 and the Endgame file. It also lets later heat-cutoff computations normalise to `spatialPartial`/`spatialSecondPartial` with a single `simp only`.
